tagline: A dual-fisheye dashcam for the Pi Compute Module 5.
summary: A headless dashcam that records continuously from a dual-fisheye USB camera, protects the footage around an impact, and serves clips to a phone over Wi-Fi. Because the two lenses sit a fixed distance apart it can also compute a depth map — on request, never while a clip is being written.
highlights: Recording is treated as the one non-optional duty: preview, depth, panorama and the web UI are all pushed off the capture thread.
Survives a camera that browns out on a bumpy road, and never fills the SD card.
Computes stereoscopic depth from the fixed-baseline dual-fisheye lenses, but only when asked, so it cannot cost frames.
Runs as a headless systemd service, and works on any Linux, macOS or Windows machine with a UVC camera — the Pi is simply where it lives in a car.

sections.heading: One rule the architecture follows from
sections.body: A dashcam that drops frames while rendering a preview is not a dashcam. Every design decision here follows from making recording the duty and everything else optional: expensive work leaves the capture thread, depth is computed on request rather than continuously, and the web interface is a reader of finished clips rather than a participant in writing them.
